annotation_description: Putting a Torch the Tower on the bottom is questionable when you could instead bottom Into the Flood Maw. Torch the Tower is efficient early removal (2 damage for 1 mana, or 3 with bargain) that pairs well with the aggressive UR tempo plan suggested by Stormchaser's Talent. Into the Flood Maw is a bounce spell that's more situational and tempo-negative (especially if you gift the fish). With only one land (Riverpyre Verge) in hand, keeping both Torch the Towers gives you better interaction against early threats and triggers prowess on the Otter from Stormchaser's Talent. The player had already bottomed one card and this was the second bottom, so they're keeping 3 cards. Keeping Riverpyre Verge + Stormchaser's Talent + Torch the Tower would have been a stronger opening than keeping Riverpyre Verge + Stormchaser's Talent + Into the Flood Maw.

With Hired Claw (a Lizard) and Burnout Bashtronaut in hand, Rockface Village would provide colored mana for creatures AND can later give Hired Claw +1/+0 and haste. Playing a basic Mountain instead misses the utility land's upside. Since the player has two more basic Mountains in hand, they won't be short on untapped red sources for future turns.

Playing a basic Mountain instead of Rockface Village when there's no reason to prefer the basic. Rockface Village enters untapped and can produce colorless or red (for creatures). Since the player has Burnout Bashtronaut to cast this turn (which costs {R}), either land works. However, Rockface Village is strictly better than a basic Mountain in this deck - it provides the same colored mana for creatures, and has an activated ability for Lizard/Mouse/Otter/Raccoon creatures. Playing the basic Mountain now means potentially drawing into a situation where you need the Village's utility later but have already used your land drop. Generally you should play the more flexible/utility land first and save basics for later, unless there's a specific reason not to (like needing to cast non-creature spells with the mana). Here the player could cast Burnout Bashtronaut with either land since it's a creature spell, and future spells like Lightning Strike need generic + red which Mountain provides. Actually, Rockface Village can only add {R} for creature spells, so for Lightning Strike ({1}{R}) you'd want a Mountain for the {R} portion. This is a minor sequencing consideration - playing Mountain is defensible since you want untapped red for non-creature spells, but playing Rockface Village now and Mountain later would leave more options open since you'd have both types available.

Using Burst Lightning to deal 2 damage to the opponent's face during combat when the Bashtronaut's combat damage will already trigger the speed increase. The burn spell doesn't provide additional speed benefit and is better saved as removal for future threats or as a finisher. At 20 life, 2 damage to face is low impact.

Using Burst Lightning to deal 2 damage to the opponent's face when they're at 20 life, rather than saving it as removal for future creatures. The Bashtronaut is already attacking unblocked so speed would likely increase from combat damage anyway. In an aggro mirror/matchup against a spell-based deck, holding instant-speed removal for future threats (like opposing creatures or to protect your own board) could be more valuable than 2 face damage this early.

GLM47 Vorthos has a Burnout Bashtronaut (1/1 menace) on board and chose not to cast Lightning Strike or attack. The opponent has only a Riverpyre Verge (a land) on the battlefield with no creatures to block. The Bashtronaut could have attacked for 1 damage for free (no blockers exist), and Lightning Strike could have been cast at the opponent's face for 3 damage, dealing 4 total damage this turn. Additionally, dealing damage would increase the Bashtronaut's speed counter, which is important for reaching max speed (double strike). Instead, they passed without attacking or casting anything, wasting 4 mana and a free attack.

GLM47 Vorthos skipped attacks into a completely empty board. With Burnout Bashtronaut (1/1) and Hired Claw (1/2) and no opposing creatures, they could have attacked for 3 damage (1 from Bashtronaut, 1 from Hired Claw's Lizard trigger, 1 from Hired Claw combat damage). This would also increase Bashtronaut's speed and enable Hired Claw's +1/+1 counter activation. Against an opponent with only 1 land and no board, there's zero risk.

Tiger-Seal is a 3/3 with vigilance but taps itself at the beginning of each upkeep, making it essentially unable to attack unless you draw a second card each turn to untap it. With only 2 lands and no reliable way to draw two cards per turn yet, Tiger-Seal will mostly just sit tapped. Stormchaser's Talent creates a 1/1 prowess Otter immediately and provides long-term value with level-up abilities, synergizing with the instant/sorcery-heavy hand (Boomerang Basics x2, Into the Flood Maw, etc.). The Otter token can also be sacrificed to bargain Torch the Tower later. Alternatively, Boomerang Basics on the Burnout Bashtronaut (which is at speed 2 and threatening to reach max speed for double strike) would buy tempo and draw a card... wait, Boomerang Basics returns a permanent to owner's hand and only draws if you controlled it. So bouncing opponent's creature doesn't draw. Into the Flood Maw could bounce the Bashtronaut (speed resets). Actually, Stormchaser's Talent seems strongest here - it gives an immediate blocker with prowess and sets up future value.

message: Promise an opponent a tapped Fish?
annotation_description: Burnout Bashtronaut has speed 2 and is progressing toward max speed (double strike), but it's only a 1/1 that costs R to replay. Hired Claw is a 1/2 that deals 1 damage whenever Lizards attack (essentially free damage each turn) and can grow with +1/+1 counters. However, the Bashtronaut's speed mechanic is persistent and doesn't reset when replayed - it will come back at the same speed level and continue scaling toward double strike, making it increasingly dangerous. That said, Hired Claw provides consistent value and is harder to deal with at 1/2 (survives more removal). The decision is close but bouncing Hired Claw may have been slightly better since it provides guaranteed damage each attack step and can grow, while Bashtronaut at speed 2 is still just a 1/1 menace for now and the opponent needs to spend mana on its pump ability to make it threatening.

GLM47 Vorthos warped Nova Hellkite for {2}{R} instead of first playing the Mountain from hand (giving 5 lands total) and hardcasting it for {3}{R}{R}. The Warp version will be exiled at end of turn, losing a permanent 4/5 flying haste threat on the board. Playing the land first would allow the full cast, keeping the dragon permanently.

Casting Nova Hellkite for its Warp cost ({2}{R}) from exile means it gets exiled at end of turn, losing a powerful 4/5 flying body permanently. The opponent is a blue-based deck with limited shown removal, so a permanent 4/5 flyer would be very difficult to deal with and represents recurring damage every turn.

message: Select a creature an opponent controls
annotation_description: Targeted Tiger-Seal (3/3) with Nova Hellkite's 1 damage ETB trigger, leaving it alive at 3/2. The Otter Token (1/1 with prowess) would have been killed outright by the 1 damage, actually removing a threat from the board. Dealing 1 damage to a 3/3 is largely inconsequential as it doesn't change relevant combat math.

Nova Hellkite is a 4/5 flying haste creature threatening 4 damage per turn, and the opponent is tapped out with all 4 Mountains tapped. Bouncing Nova Hellkite would remove the biggest threat on the board and force the opponent to re-spend 5 mana (or 3 for Warp) to replay it. Instead, bouncing Tiger-Seal to draw a card is extremely low-value — Tiger-Seal enters tapped on upkeep anyway and is a defensive creature that doesn't address the opponent's board pressure. The card draw from bouncing Tiger-Seal doesn't compensate for leaving a 4/5 flyer on the board that will continue attacking.

Casting Lightning Strike during precombat main phase is a sequencing error. If targeting the opponent's face, it should be saved for after combat or end of opponent's turn to preserve information and flexibility. If targeting the 1/1 Otter Token, it's an inefficient use of a 3-damage burn spell on a 1/1 creature when the main damage dealer (Nova Hellkite) has flying and doesn't need the path cleared.

Tiger-Seal is a ground creature that cannot block Nova Hellkite (4/5 flying), which is the primary threat at 12 life. The player should have addressed the flying threat first. Additionally, casting a spell before playing a land drop is a minor sequencing error.

The reasoning explicitly states blocking Nova Hellkite with Tiger-Seal, but Nova Hellkite has flying and Tiger-Seal cannot block it. The game system likely assigned Tiger-Seal to block a Hired Claw instead. Additionally, not also blocking with Otter Token on the second Hired Claw means taking 1 extra damage (going from 10 to potentially 5 instead of 6 after the unblockable Hellkite hits). At 10 life against an aggressive red deck, every point matters.

Casting Lightning Strike before combat when lethal damage is already available on board through attacking. Nova Hellkite (4 flying) + Sunspine Lynx (5) + Hired Claw (1 + 1 trigger) = 11 damage against opponent at 6 life with only a tapped blocker. Spending the Lightning Strike pre-combat wastes a card and removes backup burn if combat goes wrong.

GLM47 Vorthos has Lightning Strike in hand (visible in choices) and the opponent is at 3 life. Lightning Strike deals 3 damage to any target, which is exactly lethal. Instead of casting Lightning Strike to win the game, they chose to cast Razorkin Needlehead, a creature that won't resolve the game immediately. While they have attackers on board that might also be lethal, Lightning Strike is guaranteed lethal regardless of blocks or removal.
